bullets.title: Meta surges 4%+ on SemiAnalysis AI compute report; chip manufacturing in Sept
bullets.body: Meta shares rose 3–4% intraday after SemiAnalysis published a positive report on the company's AI compute business. Separately, Meta plans to begin manufacturing its own AI chip in September as part of a strategy to boost total computing power to 14 gigawatts by next year. The SemiAnalysis piece also highlighted Meta linking datacenters across 2,000 km with optical interconnects, with one analyst noting the market underappreciates optical networking as critical AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Meta faces potential $12B EU fine over addictive Instagram/Facebook feeds
bullets.body: EU regulators are pursuing Meta over addictive feed algorithms on Instagram and Facebook, with a potential fine of up to €12B. The regulatory action targets platform design practices intended to maximize user engagement.

bullets.title: Micron commits $250B to US manufacturing; New York DRAM megafab underway
bullets.body: Micron announced it will invest $250 billion in US manufacturing through 2035, building multiple 'Terafabs.' Construction on a New York DRAM megafab has already started, representing a major domestic capacity expansion commitment.

bullets.title: Photonics/optical stocks (LITE, AAOI, COHR, AXTI) testing 3-month lows
bullets.body: Photonics and optical names including LITE, AAOI, COHR, and AXTI are testing three-month lows with bulls attempting to defend support. One analyst notes it's 'too early to call a bottom' and the sector needs to hold current levels over the next few weeks to confirm any reversal. LITE is characterized as the safer/more established option versus riskier peers with higher upside potential.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo raises Western Digital PT to $730 from $575
bullets.body: Wells Fargo significantly raised its price target on Western Digital to $730 from $575, signaling a bullish view on storage demand.

bullets.title: UK designates MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, ORCL as critical third parties under financial regulation
bullets.body: The UK government designated Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Oracle as 'critical third parties,' subjecting them to direct regulatory oversight to protect the UK financial system. This is a new compliance layer for these hyperscalers operating in UK financial services.

bullets.title: H1 tech leaders nearly all red in Q3; narrow market leadership evident
bullets.body: Of the 20 top-performing S&P stocks in H1—nearly all in tech—only 2 are up in Q3, with the average return turning negative. This suggests a rotation or narrowing of leadership after the first-half rally.

bullets.title: Data center construction growth has slowed considerably
bullets.body: Multiple posts flagged that data center construction growth has slowed considerably, a potential macro headwind for chip and infrastructure plays exposed to hyperscaler capex cycles.

bullets.title: China helium export ban could pressure semiconductor supply chains
bullets.body: China imposed a temporary ban on helium exports. Helium is a critical input for semiconductor manufacturing and cooling of electronics equipment, raising supply chain risk for chip producers.

bullets.title: Oil market shrugs at US-Iran strikes; Brent near $76/bbl
bullets.body: Oil barely moved despite the US resuming strikes on Iran, with one commentator noting 'the market clearly extended the middle finger to Iran.' Brent crude fell to ~$76/bbl amid Strait of Hormuz disruptions and Qatar-mediated de-escalation talks between the US and Iran.

bullets.title: Financials and Health Care sectors flash golden cross signals
bullets.body: Both the Financials and Health Care sectors registered golden crosses (50-day MA crossing above 200-day MA with both averages rising) yesterday, a classic technical bullish signal for those two sectors.

bullets.title: ETF inflows hit $1T YTD; Goldman says volumes at 'full throttle'
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs reported that ETF ecosystem volumes are at record levels with year-to-date inflows exceeding $1 trillion, reflecting broad market participation and sustained risk appetite.

bullets.title: AAII equity allocations at 71%, well above 61.5% historical average
bullets.body: June AAII survey shows stock and stock fund allocations at 71%, significantly above the 61.5% historical average. One analyst warned investors may be extrapolating a 'very strong Q1' into future quarters without sufficient basis, raising overconfidence risk.

bullets.title: Tesla robotaxi timing debate; BYD selling 2x Tesla's volume
bullets.body: One commentator noted that even a one-year earlier Tesla robotaxi launch (June 2024 vs. 2025) would not have materially moved company financials per Elon's own admission. Separately, BYD now sells 2x Tesla's vehicle volume and makes 5x the batteries, with Chinese plants achieving manufacturing parity.

bullets.title: Top insider sales scoring red across the board; avg -24% in 90 days
bullets.body: The top 31 highest-scoring insider sales over the last 90 days are all in the red, down an average of 24%. This implies insider selling has not been a reliable bearish signal in the current rally.

bullets.title: Contrarian long JPY setup: crowded shorts meet improving Japan fundamentals
bullets.body: JPY shorts are described as crowded at a time when Japanese economic conditions, policy (Takaichi pro-growth reforms), and asset markets are shifting favorably. Large semi-government asset managers are redirecting capital domestically, adding to potential reversal pressure.

bullets.title: SK Hynix prices record $26.5B US ADR at $149/share, heavily oversubscribed
bullets.body: SK Hynix began US trading today (temp ticker SKHYV, switching to SKHY Monday), pricing its record $26.5B ADR listing at $149/share with heavy oversubscription. JPMorgan displayed the South Korean flag at its building to mark the event.
